Question: Shauna takes five tests, each worth a maximum of \(100\) points. Her scores on the first three tests are \(76,\) \(94,\) and \(87.\) In order to average \(81\) for all five tests, what is the lowest score she could earn on one of the other two tests?
Solution:
An average of \(81\) over five tests requires \(5\cdot81=405\) total points. The first three tests contribute

\[
76+94+87=257,
\]

so the last two must total \(405-257=148\) points.

To make one of those scores as low as possible, make the other as high as allowed: \(100\). The lower score can then be \(148-100=\boxed{48}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\). A lower score would force the other test above its \(100\)-point maximum.
